turns.content: Write the 25 C Nernst equation for Fe(III)+e- -> Fe(II) using free-ion concentrations, with E0=0.77 V.
At pH 1.0, use total Fe(III)=0.010 M, [H2PO4-]=6.97e-3 M, and Kf=1e21 for FeH2PO4^2+. Write the Fe(III) mass balance and formation relation, neglecting Fe(II) complexation.
Solve those relations for the free Fe3+ concentration, neglecting other phosphate complexes and treating free ligand as fixed at its stated value.
Using uncomplexed [Fe2+]=0.010 M, calculate the free [Fe3+]/[Fe2+] ratio for the Nernst quotient.
Substitute that ratio into the Nernst equation to obtain a preliminary potential.
Confirm the electron-transfer count n for Fe(III)+e- -> Fe(II) and state the corresponding 25 C Nernst coefficient.
Recompute the equilibrium ratio and potential with the electron-transfer count established in the preceding turn as a consistency check.
State the approximations that limit the precision of this calculated value.
Check the order of magnitude by expressing complexation as a downward shift in the Fe(III)/Fe(II) formal potential.
Give the final potential and explain why strong Fe(III) complexation shifts it far below E0.
